title: Orphaned Third-Party Dependency Imports
damaged_code:
```rust
// Ingesting a niche github library for a quick vacation prototype
use raw_git_library::parse_format; // No tests, zero maintainers assigned
```
pattern: Importing an external OSS package to solve a quick development problem without assigning owners to maintain it or verifying its security compliance.
why_bad: The package can easily be abandoned, leaving critical infrastructure tied to an outdated version when a security vulnerability is disclosed.
detection: A dependency library checked into the repository with zero registered code owners, failing tests, or no updates for over 2 years.
counterexample: Importing standard, heavily-vetted libraries with indefinite compatibility promises (e.g., standard library, Boost).
fix: Establish strict import rules, requiring at least two engineers to act as OWNERS to maintain and update the dependency.
source: *Software Engineering at Google (Winters et al.), Chapter 21, p. 436 [178-179, 1017-1018]*
